**Risk Officer Assessment: Recommend REFUSE (size $0)**

The coin is alive but has collapsed: down 91% from its 30-minute high, -89% over the last 15 minutes, and net sell flow of -75 SOL in that window. Sellers (743) far outnumber buyers (567), and the sell-to-buy ratio at launch was 0.98. Pool depth is only 40.7 SOL (~$7-8k), so a $20 ticket would carry heavy price impact, and a 20-50% stop would be hard to execute cleanly in a pool this thin.

The "ORGANIC" label is not reassuring: a 38% bundle share and a launch bot present cut against it. Even setting that aside, buying a coin in freefall after a 30-min high, 30-115 minutes post-graduation, falls into the base-rate range that has lost ~20% per trade.

Nothing here justifies a sane size. A skipped coin costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The brief doesn't support a buy, so the honest scout call is to pass.

The only pro-demand signals are thin. The coin is alive, classed ORGANIC, with no airdrop dump seen, and the first two minutes after graduation show about 443 buyers and 309 SOL of buying with a top-5 buyer share of 12%. Bundle share (38%) and completer share (22%) are high, though, and the last 15 minutes show the opposite of sustained demand: 743 sellers against 567 buyers, net outflow of 75 SOL, sell-to-buy ratio near 1.0 in the launch window, and a 89% drawdown from the 30-minute high. Return over 30 minutes is -80%.

Demand that was real would still be showing up as net inflow in the most recent window. It isn't. A -89% drawdown with sellers outnumbering buyers means the coin is mostly being exited, and the buyers still in are not enough to absorb it. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on top of the base rate for coins in this state, a $20 entry has no honest case.

**Call: no buy.** The scout can't make a credible argument that demand persists for the next 30-60 minutes.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a dead-cat bounce into continued distribution. The coin is already down 91% from its 30-minute high and 89% over the last 15 minutes, with net flow of -74.8 SOL and sellers (743) outnumbering buyers (567). Sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.98, so early buyers were already exiting. Pool depth is only 40.7 SOL, so a $20 round trip on a 1.4-5.1% fee/impact base would need a bounce that the flow doesn't show. Bundle share of 37.8% and a launch bot point to coordinated early supply. Top-3 holders at 12% is not a strong distribution risk by itself, but the trend is. Verdict: skip.
